title: Inverse image of Tate twists
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let
$\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$ be admissible. There are canonical
isomorphisms
$$
f^{-1}\mu_{\ell^n,Y}\cong\mu_{\ell^n,X},\qquad
f^{-1}\bigl(\Lambda_Y(d)\bigr)\cong\Lambda_X(d)\quad(d\in\mathbf Z),
$$
compatible with the isomorphism $\alpha_f\colon f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$ of
[lem-sfb-alpha-iso] and the module structures, and with the Kummer transition maps.
Consequently $f^*(K(d))\cong(f^*K)(d)$ for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Since $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring of $T=X,Y$, it is a unit of $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, so the morphisms-into-affine lemma gives a unique $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[1/\ell]$; uniqueness makes these commute with $f$. For $N=\ell^n$, affine-root representability and root-etaleness ($g=1$) put $Y\times_{\mathbf Z[1/\ell]}\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Z[1/\ell][t]/(t^N-1))$ on the small pro-etale site: etale implies ind-etale by a constant diagram, hence weakly etale, stable under base change. Apply the normalized represented-diagram comparison to $u_f$; it gives the defined root map, with group, scalar and Kummer operations. For $n=0$ both groups are trivial.

source.place: Roots of unity paragraph; Stacks sites.tex Tag 04D3 (lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf), groupoids.tex Tag 040M (example-roots-of-unity)

proof.text: Apply the torsion-system lemma with $P_{T,r}=\mu_{\ell^r,T}$ and the Step 1 maps. Clause 2 of the local-freeness theorem, with $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, supplies its reduction hypothesis. It gives all finite $A(1)$ comparisons, exponent independence and coefficient squares. The finite constant-section map is $\alpha_f$: their adjuncts agree on constant sections, so sheafification identifies them.

source.place: Finite A paragraph; Stacks sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback)

proof.text: Apply the adic-system lemma with $i=E$, $R_{E,m}=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_Y$, $S_{E,m}=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_X$, $e_E=v_{\pi_E}(\ell)$ and $M_{E,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_Y(1)$. The twist definition gives $(\ell^n)=(\pi_E^{e_En})$ and the small directed coefficient diagram. Coefficient pullback supplies $a_E=\alpha_f$. Clause 1 of local freeness, instantiated with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and site localization give the required common bases $b_n(a)=\zeta_n\otimes a$, with $t_nb_{n+1}(a)=b_n(\bar a)$. Step 2 supplies $c_{E,n}$ and their coefficient squares. The lemma yields the integral comparisons, then with $s_E=\ell$ the rational and finite-subextension colimit comparisons, all over $\alpha_f$ by coefficient-pullback clauses 2-3. Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ includes the standard coefficients.

source.place: The integral twist and Rational and algebraic closure paragraphs (compatible-local-basis route; Stacks sites.tex Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism)

proof.text: For each admissible $\Lambda$, apply the signed-line lemma with $R=\Lambda_Y$, $S=\Lambda_X$, $a=\alpha_f$, $P=\Lambda_Y(1)$, $Q=\Lambda_X(1)$ and the Step 2 or 3 comparison. The ambient twist definition supplies rank-one local freeness and identifies its signed powers and derived tensors with $\Lambda(d)$ and $K(d)$. Its module pullback is the specified $f^*$; hence the lemma gives all signed comparisons and the natural unbounded isomorphism $f^*(K(d))\cong(f^*K)(d)$, with the prescribed tensor and evaluation compatibilities.

source.place: Powers and duals paragraph; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product)
